# Construct integration changes (upstream MIT license retained)

- SimController accepts a custom grid and initial bottom/state; resources are released on exit and diagnostics are opt-in.
- `pass_poke.glsl` and `pass_probe.glsl` implement gameplay disturbances and small water-surface readbacks. `--water-check` additionally enables occasional full texture readback for diagnostics.
- `--coast-check` enables the same diagnostic readback permission. Normal gameplay still has no full-field CPU download.
- `pass_boundary.glsl` now includes Construct's `res://shaders/coastal_waves.gdshaderinc`. The renderer and wavemaker use identical incident wave components, phases, dispersion approximation and cold-start ramp. This include must accompany the vendored integration.
- The cove selects the existing mode 2 absorption strips instead of mirrored side boundaries. Pool mode 0 remains reflective, but its baked basin is now wholly inside dry padding.
- `pass_step.glsl` has an opt-in `CLOSED_BASIN` specialization (ID 0). Only the pool enables it. Cells with baked bed >= 0 m relative to resting water are closed boundaries (coping and dry upper ramp); fluid stencils reflect the corresponding physical cells across the wall, including the second ghost layer. Solid cells remain dry. The pool bake supplies wall-compatible face beds and excludes solid walls from the steep-bed desingularization neighborhood. Coastal pipelines use the default false specialization and retain the original terrain treatment.
- `pass_pool_volume.glsl` records the initial pool inventory and projects depth back to that inventory after each frame's integration. This compensates for small positivity-clamp volume errors at the shallow entry without flattening the wake. Momentum and foam mass scale with depth to preserve velocities/concentrations. The reference buffer and pipeline are created only for closed pools and released on exit; no runtime CPU readback is used.

The pool wall variant explicitly blocks water, foam and tangential advection through solid faces while retaining normal pressure. It also caps pool flow at 2.5 m/s; Construct uses a 2 ms pool timestep. The coastal cap remains 12 m/s. The KP07 interior flux, friction, foam integration and timestep algorithm are retained; the pool-only solid-wall stencil and impermeable face treatment are Construct extensions. These notes describe the integration as shipped, not an assertion that the vendor package itself has these behaviors or dependencies.
